rating_comment: The place was well maintained and the guards were super helpful. Mr Rezaul was easy to deal with and was responsive. He assisted us with all amenities and the place met out expectations. Overall it was an easy breezy stay ❤️

When i saw this flat on AirBnB, it seemed almost too good to be true. There must be a catch!
But everything was as perfect as it seemed online. Mr. Sayem and his associate Mr. Tarek is the most thoughtful, gracious host.
He provided us with all the information we needed and showed us around. The flat is just perfect!
Kitchen is compact and contains everything one needs.
The bed is comfortable, bathroom and terrace are excellent. Location is incredible.
Our main concern was the hospital (evercare) which was near to this location.
So basically the area is quiet but still close to everything you need
But They went way beyond to make our long-weekend comfortable and memorable. We will be back soon In Sha Allah

We stayed here for almost week and it has been a great experience. The house was cleaned nicely before we came in and upon request the host also managed additional parking, aerosols and few other things. The host was very cooperative and always proactive in communication. I would stay here if I come to Bangladesh again.
Nicely located very spacious, very clean, comfortable well decorated house with lots of amenities located nearby. It has the appeal of our own home. We enjoyed our stay.

I would say it is a cool, nice spacious accommodation for a large size family's vacation house. Everything is within the reach of 10-15 mins rikshaw ride. Car would take more time as usual. Mahmudur was a very accomodating host and was quick to respond to our messages.
The house was extremely spacious and clean, with lots of towels in each room. With a large supermarket about 5 minutes away from the house, it was easy for us to go out to buy groceries.

I would recommend this apartment.

An amazing stay at Mahmudur’s place. It almost felt like a home away from home. It was very clean and spacious. The netting around the building to prevent mosquitos from entering and the AC’s made it a very comfortable stay. It was well equipped with an ironing board/iron, hairdryers, fridge/freezer, washing machine/tumble dryer. Thank you for making it a pleasant and enjoyable experience.
Nice furnished house, good for 7 members families like us. Plz count the towels before use . I had to pay for 6 towels-3000 tk - don’t even know how it get lost. Thanks

all in one word is great!

Pros:
* Good location
* Spacious property
* Helpfull host & caretakers
* 24 Hrs access
* Secured and hassle free
* Plenty restaurants, shops and medicine stores around.
Cons:
* Handing over the property keys was a hassle, please keep it simple and accessible.
* 3 washrooms but no toilet tissues wew available.
* Please keep at least one towel available in each washroom.
* House WiFi signal was far too poor, requires immediate attention.
* Water leaking from the freezer/ chiller.
* Freezer/chiller was so dirty inside and stopped working at one point.
* Noisy neighbours, specially one who lived upstairs.
* Please keep the home interiors friendly and religion free.
I enjoyed staying in this property but would recommend the host to pay attention to the cons I have posted above to keep holiday makers stay more enjoyable.
Great host and awesome place! Had a wonderful time in Dhaka. Major shopping centres and amenities are nearby. All basic needs such as water and electricity were available 24/7. Easy to park as well.

The apartment was very nice and clean, just like the pictures. Air conditioning was working very well. The host was humble and accessible all the time. The only problem I felt is the elevator, as it is very small and does not work smoothly always. The apartment is in 5th floor, so a perfectly working and spacious elevator would be nice.
Everything else was perfect. The host was kind enough to put some food and water in the refrigerator. Would stay there again definitely!

Very tidy and lovely AirBnb apartment equipped with everything you need. A good bed and a nice bathroom. Iftakhar is a great host and there when you need him, Very nice and wants to share all he knows about the area. We had a great stay!
I love it

We wanted to experience the calm village life not too far from Dhaka city. This villa has met our expectations in every way. Parking was available in front of the villa. The vast front lawn had beautiful greenery including spice trees such as bay leaves and cinnamon trees. The housekeeper is available 24/7 and helped us check in and out easily. His service was exceptional, we were even able to order breakfast and tea through him! I highly recommend this home away from home.

If you need to find a peaceful place to stay in Dhaka. I recommend this place. It’s located in a residential area which means less cars and car-horn sounds! The place is near local supermarket and easy to walk around. The host is helpful and friendly!

A fantastic place, it is exacly as it says, very clean and secured. Despite being on the GF, it felt very safe. The location is good, very calm and quiet with a nice park to go for walks, (not something you can say about other parts/areas of dhaka).
You have access to a communal kitchen on a diff floor, along with Washing machine, but I didn't use those facilities, but they looked good.
Good internet, the cleaners were lovely and did a thorough job during my stay. There are stores within 5 mins walking on either direction to get all your grocery or takeaway food should you choose.
Internet is fast and reliable. Good host, good communication. The white noise is something that is true but its not frequent, none of the weekends, you are likely to hear generators in pretty much every home in dhaka. so I don't think its a massive issue given how lovely the place is. I don't watch tele, but my only suggestion should be to have a better quality tv, and a better desk chair. I am only saying this because I WFH for my entire stay, so it did get used a lot.
Overall, I do not think there's any other listing on airbnb that ticks so many boxes unless you are going for luxurious serviced apartments in dhaka.

I had a great stay and would be happy to come back and stay in this flat should I have to travel to Dhaka again. Very friendly and educated host and smiling gatekeepers. Highly recommended.

Shahid was a great host. The location of the apartment is great and it has everything you need for a stay. It is a short walk to local restaurants and amenities. The place was clean and as listed, with everything provided. It is easy to get around using the various modes of transport available. We liked it so much we booked another two nights! Thanks for making our stay a pleasurable one. Mike

wonderful stay- clean, safe and thoughtful touches for a pleasant stay

I usually do not stay at Air BnB much. But I wanted to give this place a shot and I am glad I did.
Dhaka can be a chaotic place. This place is pretty secluded inside a protected zone. Not much traffic around and pretty close to necessary amenities (I shopped at Annona mostly where you can find almost everything).
The place is very clean. You find all the needed necessities (most importantly AC in Bangladeshi hot summer). There is laundry, microwave etc. Makes you feel like home at a North American or European city.
The people are also great. Mr. Shahid is great host. But it’s the guards (Mr. Sohel and Mr. Hashem) that made the differences! I came to the place around midnight sometimes and rang the bell and they were always SMILING to open the door for me. BANGLADESHI PEOPLE ARE REALLY HOSPITABLE.
I wish them all the best and hope to stay there again next time I am in Dhaka.

I had a very good stay in the Cozy Studio. It had a bit of a musty smell at first but that disappeared after about a day. The room was clean and equipped with everything you could need and is well located, only a short journey from the airport and to Gulshan. It is also a safe and secure neighbourhood with a nice lake/park, and nearby gym and supermarket. Shahid welcomed me and gave me detailed information of anything I might need and was always quick to respond with any questions. Being on the ground floor the studio is probably the noisiest of the rooms available here but it didn't cause me too many problems.

My second time staying at this location, hope to stay here in the future. Great location, and very friendly and accomodating host. Definitely recommend.

In the future when we’re in the area will look to see if this place is available to rent. Whenever we had an issue arise, they were quick to address it and make it as if nothing happened. They were wonderful people.
Best place to stay while in Dhaka!

Niketan as a location was great, with relatively easy access to the upmarket Gulshan/Banani area, as well as the northern and eastern parts of town. Plenty of eateries and shopping around the place. A mega Aarong handicrafts store is nearby.
The apartment itself was huge - frankly, it was too large for just one person! The big TV on the wall was great - especially for the football. Sofas in the living were large and very comfy. The apartment was very clean, the air-conditioning was perfect. Kitchen was well-stocked with pots and pans. The shower in the main bathroom worked perfectly, with running hot water. The bed and pillows weren't as comfy as one might expect.
Finally, Toufiqur, the manager was extremely helpful at check-in. Farooq the caretaker was always there to help out (including opening the gate late at night!)
A really good and quiet place that had all the things needed to feel at home - super good and stable internet...

This Airbnb served as our Launchpad as we relocated to Dhaka. I recently had the best stay in Dhaka, Bangladesh, at Syd's place in Banani. The house is exceptionally nice, clean, and equipped with all the western amenities you can imagine, making it feel like I never left my home in the USA. Syd is incredibly responsive, addressing all my questions and requests within hours despite the time difference. His attentiveness and efficiency made my stay even more comfortable. I highly recommend Syd's place, especially for travelers who appreciate the convenience of being close to everything in Dhaka, while enjoying a neat and clean environment with all the necessary amenities. This is the only house I know that not only has a washer but also a dryer, so you don’t have to worry about hanging clothes on the balcony or roof. Additionally, there is a dishwasher for your dirty dishes, which is a plus for western travelers.
It's 10/10 recommended 100%.

After living for a month, I will say that this is the best service and conditions for this price. The area is clean, calm and very safe. The apartment is very spacious. The owner and caretaker will make your life as carefree and simple as possible. The only negative, not of the apartment, but of Dhaka, is mosquitoes, but in the store opposite you can buy a fumigator, which I advise you to do on the first day. Also bring earplugs, the area is quiet compared to most, but the windows in Dhaka apartments do not isolate sound 100%. Having lived in other apartments in Dhaka, for comparison I understand how good this option was for the money, it’s a pity that it was not possible to extend it, since someone booked the accommodation for the following dates.

Yum! We also had 2 breakfasts, 2 lunches, and 2 dinners, and every meal was delicious. It was also nice that dogs were welcome. Some of the photos appear to be a different place, and the boat we took was not the one pictured, but these were not dealbreakers. Overall, we had a good time and would recommend Gol Kanon to others. I had a Robi sim but Grameen works best I'm told. there's a little mobile tower not too far on the other side of the fields and walking 100 mts towards it got me 4g. the food is absolutely amazing. it's super fresh. grown locally and prepared traditionally. being a vegetarian I was worried but it turned out to be the best meals I've had in my two week Bangladesh trip. The thali we ordered was definitely worth the wait: freshly made, good quantity and it included delicious chutney and some salad. The property is dog friendly and I would definitely recommend it to anyone travelling with a pet. Follow the directions of the host, as the place is hard to find if you use only Google maps.
I would recommend to stay one more night, to explore the activities they offer and to just relax in the green oasis before heading back to Kolkata. Best stop between Siliguri and Kolkata! Recommend!

Also, the caretaker was able to provide us with additional things that we needed like a kettle, extra blankets, and Goodnight for mosquitos.
We opted for the homemade dinner option which was prepared by the host's wife. The food was delicious and I would highly recommend it if you enjoy authentic Bengali food. However, after a long day of driving and not eating on the road because we thought dinner would be ready soon after we reached, the 3 hour wait was a bit hard for us - we had an early morning the next day and ended up staying awake to eat only. Apart from this one thing (which can be improved), I would recommend this Airbnb as an affordable pet-friendly option.

This farmstead is a great, relaxing place for families to spend a few days. We were looking to get out of the city and into a more slow-paced, down to earth location. This was perfect! We were picked up at the airport and rode in a car about 40 minutes to the farmstead. We were greeted with an incredibly warm welcome. The room was large and had two double beds with plenty of room for our pack-n-play. Hot showers and a towel was provided. The hosts were gracious enough to open their kitchen and dining room to us. Home cooked meals were provided 3 times a day and they were delicious! James and his family assisted us in renting a "van" (flatbed pulled by motorized bicycle) to go explore the nearby market. Aloshikha is an absolutely amazing campus caring for a significant number of children in their on-campus orphanage, school, and hospital. We enjoyed playing games and spending time with the kids. The farmstead also had a variety of animals for our young boys to feed and play with, which they loved! We learned about the rice paddies on campus and how to grow and care for the rice plants, a unique experience! We also had the opportunity to watch the family cook on a mud stove...amazing! The sweet wife of James even baked our 4 year old a cake for his birthday! We have only compliments to give this wonderful host and airbnb! We will definitely be returning again and again!

The location was very convenient, walking distance from several food courts with English menus & a short 30tk rickshaw ride to Sonadanga bus station. The owner was very nice & did his best to be accommodating. However, honestly my stay felt like a bit of a disaster:

There was no towel, no top sheet, & half the light fixtures didn’t have bulbs (plus loose wires hanging out of a bunch of the walls). There were no lights in the stairwell at all, which was nearly pitch black (good thing I had my own flashlight) & littered with garbage. When I asked for a towel & sheet, he apologized that he’d forgotten the key to the storage closet, and told me how to get to the bazar where I could buy my own (wouldn't the right thing have been to either go get the key, or buy a towel to provide? I totally understand that mistakes happen, but it really isn't my responsibility that he left the key).

There was also no wifi. He listed a password, but it didn’t work. He said it was actually the the neighbor’s wifi, as his wifi was out due to construction or something, but the neighbor’s son must have changed the password and there’s no way to get the new one. To be fair he did eventually provide a pocket wifi with a limited data allowance, but that was a bit unexpected (I’m a web developer and the #1 criteria in choosing a place is that it has wifi; the description really should've mentioned that it isn't a true connection).

Once checked in, I headed downstairs to discover that I was locked inside the building. The gate was sealed shut with a giant padlock & I was literally trapped inside, unable to go out to get food. I called him & he came back to let me out - apparently he forgot to mention that from 11pm to 5am the gate is locked. With bars on all the windows and openings, it truly felt like jail. He apologized that he also left that key at home, so there would be no way for me to get out at night (other than to pound on a neighbor's door).

Finally, just to mention it for other guests (I knew this in advance so it’s not a complaint, but you should be aware): there’s no hot water in the shower.

I do fully recognize & understand that this is a low price for a room, but honestly, having a sheet & towel is pretty bare-minimum basic. I also understand that accidents happen re: forgetting the key. But they did have to prepare the room for the next guest at some point, right? There were pillowcases & a blanket on the bed - why not a towel & sheet? And why was a front gate key not just attached to the room key?

I booked this listing from Airbnb for 31 nights from the UK. I chose this property based on the tag “super host” and “premium property” and reviews. But I must admit it was the biggest disappointment I have faced for this trip which I thought I was getting a bargain, but I have grossly overpaid.
The property itself shown in the picture on the Airbnb website does not show the full picture. There are open electric wires hanging from the walls in the living room, dining room, and in the area near the washing machine, these are not shown in the picture and the picture was manipulated in terms of distance and lighting to hide them. The bathrooms were not cleaned properly when I first came into the property. They all have thick limescale marks in the sinks and showerheads and tiles have molds on them. In the family bathroom, there is a wooden cabinet which is very moldy and part rotten which is not very hygienic. The kitchen was also not clean, the stove and the extractor were very greasy. Much of the cutlery provided were rusted and pots have fungus on them which I had to clean to use them. The walls in the property are full of marks. In short, the property needs refurbishment and would not be described as “premium” by me. Also, there were some amenities that were not provided i.e., fire extinguisher, first aid kit, no extra bed linens, no coffeemaker, no iron, and no essentials (soap and toilet papers).
The services provided by this so-called “super host” is also extremely poor and even downright criminal because of the two major incidents I about to mention below.
The first incident I am going to talk about is the host’s attempt to take my and my son’s identity. The host came by our flat and said he needs to take copies of our passport to submit to the local council (Mirpur DOHS Parishad) for security clearance and try to justify this by comparing to how hotels check ID. Note this is after living in the property for 20 days and any ID verification needs to be informed to me before check-in which was already performed by Airbnb. The host never once mentions this before check-in and telling me that it is for security reasons for the secure area that we are living in and 20 days delay is for coronavirus. I was very suspicious when I heard this that is because the security should be more tighten since many nations are in lockdown because of the virus and not loosen it. I immediately contacted Airbnb and Airbnb advised me under no circumstance I was to hand over my and my son’s passport details to the host. The host was still insisting on getting our passport details saying they have been doing this for 2 or 3 years with every guest or at least give him our name, British address, and British phone number so that he can “negotiate” with the council. I have never heard anyone negotiate ID verification with the authorities. I have contacted Airbnb again and heard that the host informed the Airbnb that this ID verification rule came in 7 days before we check-in which is strange because the host said he had been doing this for 2 or 3 years. With these inconsistencies when confronted with the host he told me if I did not give it to him then someone from the council will come and get it. At this point, I did not trust anything this person says so I did a google search found its phone, and try to verify this by calling the council directly. No one picked the phone and no person showed up at our house to collect the passport. If this is not an example of an ID fraud scam, I do not know what is.
Having experienced seeing my friends suffer from financial fraud I will never hand over my passport to a private individual of a 3rd world country who is not a part of an accredited organization and it does not matter who he is and where he lives in PERIOD.
The second incident is where the host sent his caretaker to collect the used towels for replacement. His caretaker came and hurriedly collected all the towels for cleaning, and I did not have enough time to inspect the towels myself before it was taken. After some time, the host’s wife “Daisy” called me from the intercom and literally shouting at me for damaging her towels and at that time I told her I will pay for the damaged towels. Later when I asked the host about this, he was shouting at me saying I have put cooking marks on it and if I do not like their service, I can leave the property early. When they sent the bill of USD16.5 for the damaged items, I asked them to show me the towels I want to see the damage to verifying it which is a reasonable request. But at this time, they are gaslighting me by saying the caretaker already showed it to me which they did not, and they have thrown the towels away, so they have nothing to show me.
Wow, so they are basically falsely accusing me of damaging towels which they cannot show or have any evidence of it. This is completely unacceptable I asked them again to show me evidence and I will pay. Seeing that I am not convinced the host tried to intimidate me by attacking my knowledge on how to use towels and my mannerism so that I pay them.
There is also an incident like the caretaker once came to collect bedsheets when I went in other room to fetch the caretaker went into my bedroom and open my wardrove and inspecting my stuff without permission. This was very scary that is because I assume, they have extra keys for property

Though we've traveled to many countries around the world and many cities across USA and stayed in many hotels, we've never stayed at an Airbnb place, until now. While hotel stays are expected and known to be strictly business with formalities and superficial treatments, personal bed & breakfast and Airbnb stays are meant to be more personalized with a slightly more human touch.
While we stayed at a furnished serviced apartment place in Dhaka in the past, we really were not looking forward to staying at those types of places again simply because of poor quality and lack of 'personal' human element. We hesitated for DAYS before booking our 1st ever Airbnb stay and that also for over a month, taking the risk that if we don't like the place, we'll have to end up getting a hotel.
But Alhumdulillah/Thank God, immediately upon our arrival, we felt we made an excellent decision! Money can buy fake glitters, but not genuine human relationships. After staying here for a month, we truly felt we were related to Mr. Mannan's family.
Their hospitality is unsurpassed compared to the hospitality of any motels, hotels and bed & breakfast places we have ever stayed in; not because they provided a cleaning maid every single day, not because we had a caretaker / doorman who'd buy any essential items for us from nearby grocery or pharmacy, not also because we had a phone in the house to call the doorman or the Colonel Mannan's family anytime for anything, BUT because everyone had genuine smiles at their faces with super friendly attitude, especially the owner's family! They spoke with us as if we were their relatives and they genuinely offered to help us not only about our needs within the apartment, but also with anything in general during our stay in Dhaka.
If we ever have a need for a hotel stay in Dhaka, our 1st choice will be here.
We will miss this place and the hosts!

I arrived in Bangladesh for 7th Social Business Day, to be held July 28-29, 2017 hosted by Nobel Laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus, 3 days earlier than my reservation to Roman's place and booked a Hotel for those 3 days., so officially I was not Roman's guest however Roman is as good as review's. He guided me taking taxi from airport to his place then accompanied me to my Hotel and gave me a mobile phone with active Sim card for my needs and security that was beyond anyone's expectation.
3 days later I moved in to my reserved place (Roman's Loft). Living for 3 days in a hotel where there is a small room with 4 walls around and missing nature. Upon arriving Roman's Loft which is full of serenity, open sky, botanic environment, multi layered gardens with lots of flowers and trees, a large room with full kitchen facility above all a BOSE surrounding sound system it was great euphoric experience that any western person would love to have after a hectic, traffic jammed and sound polluted day.
During my stay I invited my other Yunus center friends and cooked food for them who were from German, Italy, Austria and Argentina. All my other Grameen Bank friends envied me for such a luxury that they didn't have or I should say they didn't choose to have.
To experience such a person and such a place's charm I am going to experience Roman's other airbnb facility as he has couple of more.
Last but not least, this place is really cool for Grameen Bank/Yonus Centre Interns or any other person who got things to do in Mirpur/Dhaka area.

Roman, the host, was the best part of my stay in Mirpur. He offered a warm welcome on arrival and provided an overall experience similar to that of visiting a relative's home.
That being said, I must be honest in my review to allow future guests have a more realistic expectation for this place.
1) This studio apartment is on the 7th floor (roof add-on) and if you don't want to take the stairs, bring a rope and climb up like Tarzan (there is no elevator).
2) Excellent Bose surround sound system was available - plug-in your media device via Aux headphone jack.
3) Beautifully decorated patio right outside of the apartment provides a 360-degree eagle view of Mirpur (you walked up 7 floors - this is your treat - take it and enjoy it)
4) Even though some of the amenities were listed as available (WiFi, hot water, etc.) you will need to communicate with Roman before your arrival to state exactly which of the amenities you will need during your stay. Wifi was made available the 2nd night because of my lack of communication. Hot water was unavailable both nights of my stay due to out of service water heater. If you need hot water, coordinate with Roman about this beforehand.
5) Mattress - I will not mention exactly what was wrong here on this public post, but I will recommend that you inspect the mattress seams/corners before you lay our body to rest for the night. I informed Roman about the issue and I am confident he will take care of it as his #1 priority.
If you are athletic and fond of a botanical living experience, this place is for you. I strongly recommend you contacting Roman ahead and discussing your needs during the stay. He speaks fluently in English and will go out of his way to help and provide a service beyond what you booked for on airbnb.

Staying with Roman was a really wonderful experience.
First of all Roman is really caring person, he does everything possible to make sure that one feels comfortable and safe. He welcomed me into his home and I got got to meet the rest of his Family, who are also great.
The flat itself is a single room with en-Suite in the top floor of the house in which Roman and his Family live. It is not luxurious but it is very clean, comfortable and private . One of the really great things about the place is that flat gives out onto a Patio from which there are a further two floors of 'balcony' giving a great view of the area and a place to relax in the evening after a long hot and tiring day in Dhaka.
The area itself is about a 1 hour (2 hours if the traffic is really bad, it is only really about 5km I think but the traffic doesn't really move in Dhaka) bus ride from downtown Dhaka {cost 25 Taka} but is interesting enough in itself and gives you a real feeling of Dhaka. There is a great Bazar on the same road as Roman's house.
I was over for the Bangladesh-England cricket ODI series and one can see the Stadium from the flat. Only a 5-10 Minute walk to the ground.
Really a fantastic experince, I am so glad I Chose to stay with Roman.
If I should visit Dhaka again I would definately want to stay with Roman.

My stay in Mahinur's place, on the rooftop of a decorative building both inside and out, was a haven of tranquility in the otherwise teeming capital of this vibrant nation. Great lengths were taken to ensure a pleasant environment with modern amenities that cater to short and long term travelers alike. I felt incredibly welcome by the thoughtful host and his family, who live just a few floors below and are only a call away. The building itself is located within walking distance of several restaurants, variety shops, bazars and cafes; those who prefer to cook their own meals will find a fully-equipped kitchen area. Getting around the city is easily accessible via a transportation hub just a few blocks away; and Mahinur can provide directions and advice, if needed.

The gem, I'd say, of the place is the 360° panoramic view of the lively Mirpur Thana (borough) from the uppermost terrace complete with seating area and a garden. If you're looking to experience Dhaka life in a local neighborhood, look no further! I extended my stay well beyond my initial dates, as I found it difficult to part with the place - and the city.

(I was a big fan of the abstract art in the stairwell.)

As I have written earlier, looking for an immersive cultural experience in Bangaldesh, I was very happy to extend my stay from 2 weeks to 4 weeks in Mahinur's loft apartment. Mahinur's brother Roman led me with assurance directly to the warm human heart of this dynamic , educated upwardly mobile nation. The flat's USP is the large terrace spaces and wide open skies six floors above bustling Bazaar road , in median class Mirpur . It is also an air-conditioned oasis that everyone needs in Dhaka. The family took me in as one of their own. Roman also extended his concern to help me feel secure about the guides, taxi and boat owners who I used in travelling the riverways in the south west, northwest, north and northeast of the Nation.

I was looking for a more immersive experience of Bangladesh and Roman has been a wonderful , communicative guide who took me right to the heart of this culturally layered , welcoming, and dynamic nation.
The flat itself is an airy , spacious, airconditioned oasis which everyone needs in the bustle of upwardly mobile, median middle class Mirpur. The sky views are its USP especially with a bit of rain. All basic conveniences are available and Roman plans to arrange for a usb wifi in the near future.
By far the most overiding element is the warmth and openhouse attitude of the host family which stays in various other floors of this building. I have extended my stay here to a full month , using it as a hub to travel the rivers and the more distant ports. In all this Roman and his contacts have helped as central co-ordinators.

The Mirpur loft experience was a unique and exciting way to witness Dhaka. The views across the city each morning were a great way to start the day and the bird's eye view of activity down below gave the space an atmospheric feel. Getting involved and witnessing daily business at the bazar, the evening street markets and all the shops, restaurants, stalls and even the mosque, (I am not Muslim), gave a terrific insight into Bangladeshi life and everyone was warm and welcoming and couldn't have been more helpful, especially as most people wanted to try out their English. I saw a cricket match at the local stadium, ate locally each day and enjoyed shopping nearby as well as using Mirpur as a base to see the rest of this amazing city. Roman and his friends and family were also a great help and couldn't have done more to ensure my stay in Dhaka was first rate and he was personally always on hand to talk about his country, the news or anything else over a cup of coffee and some home cooked food.
